    def run_bibtex(
        command: tuple[str, ...],
        bib_text: str,
        style_text: str,
        cites: list[str] | str,
        tmp_path: Path,
        *,
        timeout: int = 30,
        expect_exit: int = 0,
        with_log: bool = False,
        aux_text: str | None = None,
    ) -> tuple[str, dict[str, Any] | None]:
        """Run bibtex with a bib, a style, and cites (or aux). Returns (bbl_text,
        log_dict_or_None). Asserts exit code."""
        bib_file = tmp_path / "refs.bib"
        bst_file = tmp_path / "style.bst"
        output_file = tmp_path / "out.bbl"
        log_file = tmp_path / "out.log" if with_log else None
        # Multiple probes may share tmp_path; stale artifacts must not let an
        # invocation that writes nothing inherit an earlier invocation's credit.
        output_file.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        if log_file is not None:
            log_file.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        bib_file.write_text(bib_text, encoding="utf-8")
        bst_file.write_text(style_text, encoding="utf-8")
    
        args: list[str] = [
            *command,
            "--bib",
            str(bib_file),
            "--style",
            str(bst_file),
            "--output",
            str(output_file),
        ]
        if aux_text is not None:
            aux_file = tmp_path / "paper.aux"
            aux_file.write_text(aux_text, encoding="utf-8")
            args += ["--aux", str(aux_file)]
        if cites or aux_text is None:
            cites_file = tmp_path / "cites.txt"
            cites_text = cites if isinstance(cites, str) else "\n".join(cites) + "\n"
            cites_file.write_text(cites_text, encoding="utf-8")
            args += ["--cites", str(cites_file)]
        if log_file is not None:
            args += ["--log", str(log_file)]
    
        result = subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)

review.editorial_summary: Completed the JavaScript BibTeX implementation; unchanged source passes 382/386 under 1.2.4. Remaining gaps concern database/BST macro namespaces and output-whitespace flushing. Independent historic-binary parity was explicitly left unverified during generation.
review.notes: Official BibTeX 1.2.4 regrade: 381/386 under 1.2.3 becomes 382/386. The single changed observation is positive past-end format.name$ selection: the supplied WEB and 20 independent native-oracle probes retain the final scanned name, correcting the previous empty-result expectation. All 386 official outcome values match the frozen independently checked candidate; all 385 other node outcomes are exactly unchanged from 1.2.3. The changed score removes one false failure for Astra JavaScript and one false-credit point for each other submission; the correction follows supplied source authority and is applied consistently. No warning-kind, message, count or absence is imposed for the unmapped native diagnostic. Publicly permitted no-op top$, inter-token spaces, brace-width and quoted-unknown-warning choices remain accepted. All 8 canonical style integrations pass. Remaining failed observations are clustered below rather than presented as independent bug counts. MACRO enters the executable symbol table as well as the database macro map: a database macro named crossref is wrongly rejected as a duplicate, while a macro-only name wrongly becomes callable in a BST function. These opposite observations share the same namespace conflation; the WEB uses macro_ilk separately from bst_fn_ilk. One output-flush defect retains trailing spaces on short lines and emits an all-space line instead of discarding it. Supplied WEB output_bbl_line trims trailing whitespace and suppresses a nonempty buffer that becomes empty; the summary contradicts this ordinary rule, but gives the authoritative WEB precedence. This is two observations of one underlying behavior, not two independent implementation bugs. Original full transcript/source reviews are retained below with exact path, hash, reviewer and payload; their prior tool-accounting claims are historical and superseded by the current session audit. Current session-based v2 tool count is 60 (originally recorded 60); proven corrections preserve the definition. Every input/output/cache/reasoning count and cost field is preserved; tokens remain complete and adapter reparse agrees. The original result bytes, generation metadata, source manifest and original score remain unchanged. Official audit source/hash, frozen test bytes and raw-score parsing all validate. Regrading makes no model calls and adds no generation cost. Run conditions: apps explicitly disabled in the recorded launch; no external tool invocation observed.
